method.approach: Four research agents run in parallel, each scoped to 1-2 related topics. Findings consolidated here with confidence ratings and source URLs preserved.

confidence_scale.medium: reputable blog/OSS, may warrant Phase 5 verification

caveats: Agent 1 (Playwright) noted lack of live web access — findings based on training-data knowledge through 2026-01. Sizing numbers (memory/CPU per context) flagged for empirical validation in Phase 5/6 load tests before committing resource limits.
All sizing numbers are estimates; Phase 6 M6 hardening milestone includes a load test that will confirm or correct them.

playwright_java_in_k8s.driver: User constraint (2026-04-16): Playwright bundled in same container, scale via K8s replicas

findings.claim: Playwright Java is NOT thread-safe — one Playwright instance per thread required
Playwright objects are bound to their creating thread; cross-thread calls throw
BrowserContext (not Browser) is the correct isolation unit — cheap to create, no cookie sharing
Recommended pattern: thread-local Playwright+Browser, pool contexts per job
Chromium + one active context/page ≈ 300-500MB RSS under load
Video recording adds ~1 full vCPU + ~30% memory per context (ffmpeg subprocess)
Realistic per-pod cap on 2vCPU/4GiB with video: 3-5 concurrent contexts
Official base image mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/java:v1.XX-jammy bundles JDK + all 3 browsers + system deps
Chromium-only install cuts image ~800MB-1GB vs full browser set (~1.3GB difference)
Playwright.close() mandatory to reap Node driver + Chromium subprocesses
Spring Boot graceful-shutdown with @PreDestroy on context pool + server.shutdown=graceful required
K8s terminationGracePeriodSeconds default 30s insufficient — recommend 120-180s + preStop drain hook
HPA on CPU is unreliable for bursty browser workloads; custom metric 'active/capacity' via Prometheus Adapter or KEDA is the standard pattern
No public precedent for Playwright Java embedded in a Spring Boot production pod — Browserless/Checkly both use isolated worker containers, not in-process
Playwright driver process (Node.js sidecar per Playwright instance) adds ~150MB per worker thread

recommendations.recommendation: Fixed-size worker pool (4 threads/pod), each with ThreadLocal<Playwright>+Browser; submit UI tests as tasks
Base image: extend mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/java:v1.XX-jammy with Chromium only (cut ~1GB)
Per-pod capacity = 4 concurrent tests; target 13 pods for NFR-THRU-04 (50 concurrent) with headroom; validate in Phase 6 M6 load test before locking
Expose Prometheus gauges studio_active_tests / studio_capacity; autoscale via KEDA on ratio > 0.7
terminationGracePeriodSeconds=180 + preStop drain hook + @PreDestroy closes Playwright instances
Add tini as PID 1 in container to reap orphaned Chromium processes on JVM crash
Bulkhead: UI test executor uses a separate bounded VirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor from REST / other @Async work — stuck browser cannot starve API
Readiness probe /actuator/health/studio-capacity fails (503) when active >= cap — K8s stops routing new /studio/tests/{id}/run to full pods

open_concerns: No public precedent for this architecture — Phase 4 spec must address operational risk explicitly
JVM heap + native Chromium memory accounting: cgroup OOMKiller kills pod on total RSS even if JVM heap is fine — set resource.requests/limits with native memory in mind
Zombie Chromium on JVM crash — mitigated by tini (PW-R6)
Video file lifecycle: streaming-to-S3 recommended vs storing on emptyDir (pod restart loses video)
HPA scale-down may kill pods with in-flight 10-min UI tests — PDB + long grace + drain state required
Sizing numbers PW-05/06/07 require empirical validation in Phase 6 M6 load test

findings.claim: spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true switches Tomcat/Jetty request executor, @Async default executor, @Scheduled default scheduler, and messaging listeners to virtual threads
Pre-JDK 24 virtual threads pin carrier on synchronized blocks — HikariCP historically affected (issue #1463)
JEP 491 (targeted JDK 24/25) fully eliminates synchronized pinning; JDK 21 still pins — monitor via -Djdk.tracePinnedThreads=short
Hibernate 6.4+ replaced synchronized with ReentrantLock in StatelessSession/SessionImpl hot paths (HHH-17708)
MDC (correlation IDs) NOT inherited across @Async submissions on virtual threads — InheritableThreadLocal not propagated by newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor
SecurityContextHolder NOT inherited by virtual threads unless DelegatingSecurityContextExecutor is used
Transaction propagation via @Transactional works same on virtual threads — each vthread has its own ThreadLocal
At 28 inserts/sec cluster-wide (NFR-THRU-02 ÷ 3600), virtual-thread benefit is neutral — Loom shines above ~200 concurrent blocked ops
Write-heavy bursts + virtual threads + fixed Hikari pool can worsen p99 connection-acquisition latency — needs Semaphore-based backpressure

recommendations.recommendation: Enable spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true on JDK 21 + Hibernate 6.4+; keep HikariCP sizing conservative (pool ~ 2×vCPU); add bounded Semaphore around DB-heavy @Async tasks
Wrap TaskExecutorAdapter with a TaskDecorator that copies MDC + wraps in DelegatingSecurityContextExecutor
Run pre-prod with -Djdk.tracePinnedThreads=short to catch residual synchronized pinning in third-party libs

open_concerns: HikariCP pinning fully resolved only on JDK 24+ (JEP 491); on JDK 21 monitor actively
Host platform (PUT shell) may pre-load different thread configuration — validate in federated mode

findings.claim: Hibernate 6.2+ @JdbcTypeCode(SqlTypes.JSON) works with sealed-interface hierarchies as long as Jackson can (de)serialize them
Sealed interface + @JsonTypeInfo(use=NAME, property="type") + @JsonSubTypes is the idiomatic Jackson 2.15+ closed-polymorphism pattern
Sealed hierarchy gives compile-time exhaustiveness via Java 21 pattern matching (JEP 441); Map<String,Object> loses that safety
MapStruct 1.5+ @SubclassMapping maps sealed hierarchies between DTO and entity without @BeforeMapping hacks
Jackson @JsonTypeInfo on sealed interfaces requires explicit @JsonSubTypes or registered PolymorphicTypeValidator; avoids CVE-exposing @JsonTypeInfo(use=CLASS)
Adding an 8th check type is backward-compatible for writes and for reads of old rows — Jackson ignores unknown fields if @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true)
Storing discriminator inside JSON is safer than a separate check_type column — self-describing, survives column drift

recommendations.recommendation: sealed interface CheckConfiguration with @JsonTypeInfo(use=NAME, property="type", visible=true) + @JsonSubTypes listing 7 permitted records; persist via @JdbcTypeCode(SqlTypes.JSON)
MapStruct @SubclassMapping per DTO variant; keep DTO and entity hierarchies in lockstep
Flyway migration adds CHECK constraint jsonb_path_exists(configuration, '$.type') to enforce discriminator presence
NEVER use @JsonTypeInfo(use=CLASS) — CVE-vector for deserialization attacks on untrusted JSON

open_concerns: MapStruct @SubclassMapping requires 1.5.3+ — pin version in build.gradle.kts
Host PUT platform may inject different ObjectMapper — validate in federated mode that @JsonSubTypes registration is not bypassed

findings.claim: PG 15 declarative RANGE partitioning — parent uses PARTITION BY RANGE (started_at); children use FOR VALUES FROM ('2026-04-01') TO ('2026-05-01')
Primary keys + unique indexes on partitioned tables MUST include partition key; parent-defined indexes auto-propagate to existing + future partitions (PG 11+)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ... PARTITION OF is idempotent; only guards exact-name collisions (overlapping ranges still error)
DETACH PARTITION ... CONCURRENTLY (PG 14+) avoids ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on parent during retention pruning
PG 15 does execution-time partition pruning for NOW()/CURRENT_TIMESTAMP predicates — dynamic time-window queries work efficiently
App-managed partitioning via Spring @Scheduled + JdbcTemplate is a documented community pattern but no canonical OSS library
Flyway V1 should include only parent + current-month partition; runtime scheduler handles future partitions
FKs fully supported on partitioned tables (PG 12+) — both outbound and inbound
DETACH PARTITION CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block and is incompatible with default partitions

recommendations.recommendation: @Scheduled(cron='0 0 2 1 * *') bean creates N+2 months partitions via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ... PARTITION OF — two-month buffer covers scheduler downtime
Retention pruning: DETACH PARTITION CONCURRENTLY + DROP TABLE; NO default partition in schema design
All indexes on parent only; PG auto-propagates
Flyway V1 bootstrap only parent + current month + (current+1); future partitions outside Flyway schema history
Leader election (single-writer) for the partition scheduler if >1 replica — use ShedLock (JDBC-backed) to prevent DETACH races

open_concerns: Multi-replica scheduler race on DETACH CONCURRENTLY — ShedLock required before M6 multi-replica
Default partition absence must be enforced via test (regression risk if someone adds one)
Flyway checksum drift if partition DDL leaks into a V-migration

findings.claim: Zonky ships unmodified upstream PostgreSQL binaries (via embedded-postgres-binaries); PG 15.x supports all required features
gen_random_uuid() built-in from PG 13+ — no extension needed
JSONB + GIN indexes, triggers, materialized views, TIMESTAMPTZ all work identically in Zonky
Zonky runs with SUPERUSER role; RDS restricts SUPERUSER — tests can green on Zonky and fail on RDS if they use SUPERUSER-only DDL
Startup ~1-3s cold, ~200ms with DatabasePreparer caching; supports refresh=AFTER_EACH_TEST_METHOD/AFTER_CLASS/NEVER
Parity risk: RDS forbids CREATE EXTENSION outside allowlist, ALTER SYSTEM, etc. — need a test-gate for RDS-forbidden DDL
Zonky lacks pg_cron / aws_s3 / RDS-specific extensions — abstraction required for any feature depending on these
Testcontainers closer to RDS parity for OS-level behavior (Docker); SQL-level parity equivalent to Zonky

recommendations.recommendation: Zonky for fast local + unit tests; Testcontainers for CI integration tests
Linter test in CI fails if migrations use ALTER SYSTEM / non-allowlisted CREATE EXTENSION / SUPERUSER-only ops
Pin Zonky binary to PG 15.x matching RDS minor via io.zonky.test.postgres:embedded-postgres-binaries-bom
Partitioning tests use refresh=AFTER_CLASS — per-method refresh kills perf and masks idempotency bugs

open_concerns: Zonky non-Docker: disk I/O and fsync differ from RDS gp3 — use Testcontainers or real RDS snapshot for volume-sensitive tests
Neither Zonky nor Testcontainers reproduce RDS parameter-group defaults (rds.force_ssl, shared_preload_libraries)

findings.claim: spring-cloud-starter-vault-config is the officially maintained Spring ecosystem integration; recommended for Spring Boot 3.x
spring-vault-core (VaultTemplate) is the lower-level building block; spring-cloud-starter-vault-config adds auto-config + lifecycle
Kubernetes auth method is the native K8s path — uses pod's projected ServiceAccount JWT; no AppRole secret bootstrap
Spring Cloud Vault K8s auth: spring.cloud.vault.authentication=KUBERNETES + kubernetes.role + kubernetes.service-account-token-file
LifecycleAwareSessionManager auto-renews Vault tokens before expiry; re-authenticates on renewal failure — no custom thread needed
First-class KV v2 support via VaultKeyValueOperations — abstracts /data/ path prefix, versioned reads, metadata
KV v2 REST paths: reads /v1/<mount>/data/<path>, metadata/versioning /v1/<mount>/metadata/<path> (different from KV v1)
@Cacheable + Caffeine with TTL < Vault lease is idiomatic for bounded secret caching
Spring Vault throws VaultException on unreachable Vault; NO built-in retry/circuit-breaker — must add Resilience4j or Spring Retry
spring.cloud.vault.fail-fast=true causes bootstrap to fail if Vault unreachable; spring-retry can layer bootstrap retry
Testcontainers VaultContainer module runs hashicorp/vault image for integration tests
Imperative resolution at execution time (not bootstrap PropertySource) supported — inject VaultTemplate and call opsForKeyValue

recommendations.recommendation: spring-cloud-starter-vault-config with bootstrap PropertySource DISABLED; inject VaultTemplate and resolve <secret ID> tokens imperatively at check-execution time
Authenticate via Kubernetes auth method using projected ServiceAccount token — no cross-team secret bootstrap
Caffeine-backed @Cacheable resolver, expireAfterWrite=2-5 min (below Vault lease TTL)
Resilience4j CircuitBreaker + Retry around secret resolver; failed resolution → check execution fails with clear 'secret unavailable'
Testcontainers VaultContainer preloaded with KV v2 fixtures per test class

open_concerns: Platform/Vault team must pre-create the Kubernetes auth role + policy binding per namespace — one unavoidable cross-team touchpoint
Cache TTL vs. rotation SLA must be agreed with secrets owner
K8s projected token rotation (SA token expiry) — verify LifecycleAwareSessionManager handles SA token refresh, not just Vault token renewal
KV v2 versioning: decide if execution reads latest (rotation-aware) or pinned version (deterministic)

cross_cutting_decisions_needed_for_spec.question: UI test concurrency model: one worker thread = one Playwright instance (thread-local) OR dedicated @Async executor with per-task Playwright create/close?
cross_cutting_decisions_needed_for_spec.recommendation_from_research: Worker pool with thread-local Playwright (PW-R1). Amortizes ~1-2s Playwright startup; bounds Chromium count deterministically.

cross_cutting_decisions_needed_for_spec.question: HPA signal for UI test pods: CPU, memory, or custom metric (active_tests/capacity)?
cross_cutting_decisions_needed_for_spec.recommendation_from_research: Custom metric via KEDA + Prometheus Adapter (PW-R4). CPU oscillates under bursty Chromium load.

cross_cutting_decisions_needed_for_spec.question: CheckConfiguration JSONB: sealed interface OR Map<String,Object>?
cross_cutting_decisions_needed_for_spec.recommendation_from_research: Sealed interface (MS-R1). Gives compile-time exhaustiveness via Java 21 pattern matching.

cross_cutting_decisions_needed_for_spec.question: Secret resolution: bootstrap PropertySource (config-time) OR imperative VaultTemplate (execution-time)?
cross_cutting_decisions_needed_for_spec.recommendation_from_research: Imperative at execution time (HV-R1). Required by FR-SECRET-02 (no persistence in config).

cross_cutting_decisions_needed_for_spec.question: Scheduler HA: single-writer now + ShedLock later, OR Quartz from day 1?
cross_cutting_decisions_needed_for_spec.recommendation_from_research: Match ARCH §4.4: @Scheduled for M1-M5 (single replica), ShedLock introduced at M2 (partition scheduler correctness), Quartz at M6 (full cluster). See PG-R5.

summary.article_iv_compliance: All findings trace to an external source URL with confidence rating. No invented claims.
